primary_claim: Analyzing 17 benchmarks (~110 datapoints) from the Epoch AI Benchmarking Hub for when open-weight models first cross score thresholds relative to closed models, open models are currently roughly 8-10 months behind the closed frontier on private benchmarks and roughly 4-6 months behind on public benchmarks, with the gap smallest around DeepSeek R1 (Jan 2025) and growing since; public benchmarks underestimate the gap by roughly a factor of two relative to private ones.

effect.metric: backward-looking delay (months) between closed and open model first-crossing of benchmark score thresholds
effect.value: private benchmarks: ~8-10 months gap; public benchmarks: ~4-6 months gap; gap minimal around Jan 2025 (DeepSeek R1) and growing since; public benchmarks underestimate the gap by close to a factor of two relative to private

stated_future_work: estimate winner's-curse bias in the gap measurement more carefully, e.g. using the ECI framework
further investigate whether real-world task gaps are larger than measured benchmark gaps, given open developers' apparent lesser access to varied enterprise data and feedback
limitations_stated: old data from 2023-2024 is partially self-reported; several 'private' benchmarks are not fully private

methodology assumes benchmarks tested all major open and closed models, which is not typically the case; judgement calls (made partly by Claude Opus 4.7, partly overruled by the human authors) were needed to accept/reject datapoints
winner's-curse bias: first models to cross a threshold tend to be positive fluctuations, which could favor closed models since benchmarks typically run more closed models
provider degradation when serving open models through third-party providers with zero-data-retention could bias the measured gap to be larger

FrontierMath's OpenAI funding/access and ARC-AGI's semi-private/API-exposed set both create contamination risks that inflate the closed-model side specifically, which would overstate rather than understate the true gap

the 'reasoning' benchmark category shows a larger gap but all three constituent benchmarks are private, so category effects are confounded with public/private status; not enough data to draw firm category-level conclusions
quote: We find that, as of today, on private benchmarks, where the data is not publicly accessible, open models are roughly 8-10 months behind the closed frontier, while for public benchmarks the gap is roughly 4-6 months.
